The Nocturnals

Something already knows where tonight is.

Coyotes know the night through passages: the lane that still goes through, the gate that no longer does, the room audible only around the next corner. Terminal City calls these scouts the Nocturnals. They can try a familiar route and find it shut. They can find another. A person who notices may follow, but the choice belongs to the person. The animal has more of the night to cover.

The coyote reaches its usual bramble gap and finds new growth across it. It backs away from the thorns, pauses with one paw on damp ground, and follows a faint cadence along the fence. At a dry excavation seam, that cadence cuts out. The late-shift worker, already lost, watches from a distance as the animal tests the closed side, retreats and chooses an ordinary lane around the works. At the next damp verge the cadence returns changed. A corner appears a little nearer in the second view, though the coyote has performed no trick. The worker elects to take the same public lane. A moth crosses a steady entrance light; bass finally becomes audible, and the host opens the warehouse door. The worker enters. The coyote passes beyond the gathering and continues its own night.

The ruleA guide can find a way. It cannot make you take it.

Terminal City · Storybook v0.10.0 · built 2026-09-13
Terminal City is an original fictional mythology inspired by Vancouver’s geography, weather, wildlife, infrastructure, art, and electronic music. It makes no claim to historical, Indigenous, or religious tradition. Real places are used as settings; the operating system layered on them is invented.
Made by Steve Hiehn, a software developer and electronic musician based in Vancouver, Canada. All music was created using a custom DAW, Signals & Sorcery.
